correctness.rationale: For integrable \(X,Y\), rewrite the source terms as \(A=\mathbb E[(Y-X)\mathbf 1_{\{X<Y\}}]\) and \(B=\mathbb E[(X-Y)\mathbf 1_{\{X>Y\}}]\). Then \(A-B=\mathbb E(Y-X)\) exactly because the equality event contributes zero. Therefore \(A\ge B\) if and only if \(\mathbb E X\le\mathbb E Y\). No independence or distributional regularity is used; zero-probability strict-comparison events are covered by the truncated-expectation formulation.
